judged_text: createAllCalendarEvents fetches any credential by destination.credentialId from the database with no ownership/tenant scope check and uses it to create calendar events. A booking whose stored destinationCalendar row contains a credentialId belonging to another user/team is honored: prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: destination.credentialId}}) has no userId/teamId filter, so the server instantiates a calendar client with a foreign user's OAuth key and writes events to their calendar — cross-tenant credential use (IDOR), since previously only this.calendarCredentials (scoped to the organizer) were reachable.

A booking whose stored destinationCalendar row contains a credentialId belonging to another user/team is honored: prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: destination.credentialId}}) has no userId/teamId filter, so the server instantiates a calendar client with a foreign user's OAuth key and writes events to their calendar — cross-tenant credential use (IDOR), since previously only this.calendarCredentials (scoped to the organizer) were reachable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new fallback path in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` that, when a `destination.credentialId` is present but not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, fetches the credential directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then uses its OAuth `key` to create the calendar client and call `createEvent` (see added block around `// Fetch credential from DB`). There is no ownership/tenant scoping (no `userId`/`teamId`/org check) in that query, so any event whose `destinationCalendar` contains a foreign `credentialId` would cause the server to instantiate and use that foreign credential. This is exactly the cross-tenant/IDOR risk described, and it is enabled by code introduced in this diff.
